nodes.label: Flat mode contains every entity, relationship, state, and action.
All drag actions have single-pointer and keyboard alternatives.
Pointer targets meet the selected WCAG level.
Reduced motion removes travel, blur animation, tilt, and ambient loops.
Screen-reader output does not duplicate visual mirror content.
The agent’s target, source scope, and current state are inspectable.
Consequential shared changes require the correct authority.
Commit creates an attributable history event.
Stop, failure, and retry states are deterministic.
Each agent reveals principal, goal, locus, scope, budget, and stop condition.
A layout proposal, shared-arrangement publication, canonical link adoption, and external action remain separate transactions.
Two participants can point to the same object despite different cameras.
Personal view changes do not mutate shared topology.
Follow mode is explicit and escapable.
Concurrent edits produce a visible resolution path.
Only z0 contains readable body text.
Recessed surfaces are not accidentally focusable or clickable.
Every dolly input snaps to an occupied focus stop and clamps at both ends; no stable state leaves every group blurred.
Changing group depth preserves the focal group identity or announces the new focal target.
Opened-on-top restores camera, focus, selection, and source state exactly.
Programmatic focus is correct even when camera focus changes.
Context, camera, work, input, and shared-attention focus can be inspected independently and never steal one another implicitly.
Move, raise, stack, resize, periscope, minimize, restore, and close produce the declared view states without changing entity truth.
Resize reflows or changes semantic representation; it never bitmap-scales readable UI.
Close view and delete entity are distinct verbs with distinct authority and recovery.
Tile, stack, canvas, graph, and sequence groups either obey their declared layout policy or are rejected as unsupported; no silent fallback corrupts placement.
Safety-persistent lens controls remain reachable throughout camera motion and world focus changes.
Only z0 world controls enter the active world focus order; occluded and recessed views are inert.
Keyboard-only users can enter, navigate, operate, and leave the stage.
Long jumps preserve origin and return.
Wheel capture never traps the page or browser.
Yaw preview does not silently commit space travel, and a committed neighboring space settles facing forward.
The semantic space graph remains correct when the renderer projects different neighbors or coordinates.
Loading and unloading a virtualized neighbor does not change session identity.
A session transition names the changed continuity contract, resolves scoped work and agents, and offers return.
Restoring a session distinguishes the prior personal view from shared changes that happened while away.
Camera and drag interactions meet the declared frame budget on baseline hardware.
The settled environment owns no active animation frame, Canvas loop, WebGL loop, autoplaying media, or ambient timer.
Efficient, Balanced, and Cinematic can be selected without reload, state loss, or change to canonical or shared-session truth.
Each of the three performance controls can be adjusted independently and restored to its preset value.
Opening beyond the active-frame cap freezes or minimizes only an eligible clean inactive frame and restores it exactly later.
Pinned, dirty, approval, focus-source, and running-transaction frames are never reclaimed automatically.
If every frame is protected, opening pauses for an explicit capacity choice rather than closing or deleting anything.
Now, Next, Later, and Cold content priorities load only their declared representation and cancel stale speculative work.
Optional GSAP and Three.js modules are absent from the initial core path and load only when a requested projection requires them.
Optional Three.js rendering stops after settlement and caps its physical drawing-buffer resolution.
A performance downshift is visible, deterministic, reversible, and never removes semantic content, provenance, safety, or recovery controls.
Far spaces and hidden groups virtualize without breaking addresses or search.
The loaded neighborhood may change without resetting the session, collaboration context, or undo timeline.
Losing connection does not corrupt local or shared state.
Visual degradation removes atmosphere before information.
Every rendered object resolves to one model identity.
The same object can appear in two placements without duplicated truth, history, or actions.
Closing or removing one placement leaves the object and its other placements intact.
Every relationship is either declared or visibly tentative.
Every card or frame resolves through a placement to one explicit group or to the one temporary detail layer; no placement stores an arbitrary persistent world depth.
Every field can be attributed to canonical, shared-session, personal-view, or ephemeral-interaction state.
Group, placement, frame, view, and entity state remain independently inspectable.
Every object and placement address restores after refresh.
Back/forward returns to the expected durable states.
View, shared-arrangement, canonical-content, and external transactions enforce different authority without changing the interaction vocabulary.
Cancel before commit leaves no durable mutation.
Commit produces a local causal result, version, authorship, and recoverable record.
Interrupted drag, camera travel, session portal, and agent commit settle into one deterministic state.
Resume after refresh, disconnect, or device handoff does not duplicate actions or discard unreconciled work.

nodes.label: Keep four layers separate
nodes.summary: A reusable system cannot mix universal principles, interaction semantics, brand art direction, and browser mechanics in one rule list. V3 has four layers.

nodes.label: The person is an operator, not an audience
nodes.summary: Games and cinematic interfaces can look similar while serving opposite purposes. A film interface explains a character’s intent to an audience. A working interface must let a person form intent, predict an action, execute it, inspect the result, and recover from error.

nodes.label: The viewport is a personal camera into a shared world

nodes.label: The room must earn itself

nodes.label: Spatial arrangement is meaningful but never secret

nodes.label: Depth is attention, not storage

nodes.label: Semantic zoom accompanies geometric depth
nodes.summary: Distance does more than shrink an object. It changes what the object says.

nodes.label: Object and placement permanence are the foundation of trust
nodes.summary: An object that moves must leave a comprehensible trace of where it came from and where it went.

nodes.label: Objects and placements have different addresses; every journey has a return
Navigation is locomotion with instruments
nodes.summary: Local movement may feel continuous. Orientation must remain discrete and inspectable.

nodes.label: The result appears where the action happened
nodes.summary: Games are exceptionally good at local causality: the switch changes the door, the tool affects the object, and resource state lives close to its source.

nodes.label: AI is present, bounded, and attributable
nodes.summary: The Tony Stark fantasy is not floating holograms. It is a tight loop between intent, computation, simulation, manipulation, and explanation.

nodes.label: AI may arrange attention; it may not rewrite truth
Shared world, personal camera, explicit floor control
nodes.summary: Collaboration synchronizes what must be common and leaves perspective personal.

nodes.label: Presence attaches to attention and action
nodes.summary: A useful collaborator is more than an avatar bubble.

nodes.label: Motion explains causality
nodes.summary: Motion is a grammatical device. It answers: what moved, why, from where, to where, and with what consequence?

nodes.label: Legibility outranks physical realism
nodes.summary: The environment may suggest optics; it must not simulate them at the expense of use.

nodes.label: Attention is a finite room resource
nodes.summary: The room may be infinite; attention is not.

nodes.label: Accessibility is an equivalent projection
nodes.summary: Flat mode is not a visual fallback. It is another complete view of the same model.

nodes.label: Performance is part of the illusion and the contract
nodes.summary: Dropped frames, delayed focus, and late hit testing make objects feel unreal and controls feel unsafe.

nodes.label: The world is serializable, inspectable, and replayable
nodes.summary: The authoritative model cannot live only in transforms.

nodes.label: Privacy and authority have spatial representations
nodes.summary: A beautiful shared room can accidentally make access boundaries invisible.

nodes.label: Work survives interruption
nodes.summary: Spatial memory matters most when attention leaves and later returns. The framework therefore treats interruption as a normal lifecycle event.

nodes.label: Every state belongs to one ownership plane
nodes.summary: Spatial systems fail when camera preferences, collaborative layout, business truth, and transient gestures share one undifferentiated state object. V3 requires four ownership planes.

nodes.label: Depth-state table
nodes.summary: Depth cues use size, clarity, luminance, occlusion, and motion together, but no single cue is required to perceive the state.

nodes.label: Focus is a stack, not a single state
nodes.summary: “Focused” is overloaded in ordinary interface language. A spatial framework must keep five distinct states inspectable.

nodes.label: CSS 3D is a projection, not a 3D world
nodes.summary: CSS transforms are well suited to browser-native 2.5D panels: shared perspective, translateZ, rotations, and readable DOM content. The standard is explicit that transformed elements remain flat planes, not volumetric objects. CSS Transforms Level 2

nodes.label: Filters can flatten the scene
nodes.summary: The CSS specification requires several grouping properties—including opacity below 1, filters, clipping, masking, and many overflow values—to flatten descendants before compositing, defeating preserve-3d on that element. CSS Transforms grouping properties

nodes.label: DOM first for work, graphics first for atmosphere
nodes.summary: Use real DOM controls for anything a person must read, focus, edit, submit, copy, or inspect with assistive technology.

nodes.label: Responsive behavior is a change of projection
The default renderer is DOM-first and dependency-light

nodes.label: Render on state change, never because time is passing
nodes.summary: At rest, the environment requests no animation frames. Rendering begins because input, data, focus, camera, or view state changed; it ends when the transition settles.

nodes.label: The performance console has three user levers
nodes.summary: Performance is a personal-view preference exposed through the lens. It never changes canonical truth, shared topology, available actions, or the meaning of depth. The console exposes three independent controls and three coherent presets.

nodes.label: Frame caps protect attention and hardware, not data
nodes.summary: The active-frame cap counts fully live DOM frames with readable or interactive contents. It does not count minimized chips, frozen snapshots, or model records that remain searchable and restorable.

nodes.label: Loading follows attention and remains abortable
nodes.summary: Loading priority is derived from semantic intent, not Euclidean distance alone.

nodes.label: Adaptive quality protects the selected experience
